whatItDoes: Calculates simple interest on a principal amount over a period of years. Unlike compound interest, interest is only ever calculated on the original principal, so you can see the total interest and final amount clearly.
whyItExists: Simple interest is used for many personal loans, promissory notes, and short-term lending. Seeing the total interest and final amount makes the true cost of borrowing — or the return on lending — transparent.
whoShouldUse: Borrowers of simple-interest personal loans, savers with simple-interest deposits, and finance students checking their math.

Enter the exact time in years (use fractions for partial years if needed)

commonMistakes: Using a compound-interest formula for a simple-interest loan
Entering months instead of years without converting
Applying the rate to the growing balance
Forgetting that late fees can change the total
Assuming all personal loans use simple interest when some compound
faq: What's different from compound interest? — Interest is only charged on the original principal, never on accumulated interest.
What uses simple interest? — Many personal loans, auto notes, and short-term instruments.
How do I convert months? — Enter months/12 as the time in years.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Why is simple interest lower than compound? — Because it never earns interest on interest, so the total grows only from the original principal.
Can a loan be simple interest but still have fees? — Yes, fees are usually separate from the interest calculation.
